channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: pARTy 'til the Cows Come Home · The Firefly Artists
item.description: 5th annual juried exhibition from Long Island artist cooperative The Firefly Artists heralding Northport's Great Cow Harbor Day Weekend — a "moo-ving" celebration of cows, farm life, the Cow Harbor 10K race weekend, and the Village of Northport itself. Street photography of Cow Harbor Weekend is particularly appreciated, and all original 2D and 3D media up to 36"×36" are accepted, photography included. First through third place and honorable mention awards; exhibition at the gallery at 90 Main Street August 26 – September 27, 2026, with reception September 17 during race week. All work for sale, 35% commission. — Deadline: August 5, 2026. Fee: $35 (+$5 each addl). Prize: Gallery exhibition + 1st-3rd place awards.

item.title: Inspired by Cape Cod · Cape Cod Art Center
item.description: Summer online all-media exhibit from Cape Cod Art Center inviting photographers and studio artists to submit work inspired by Cape Cod — its light, landscapes, and life. Up to 5 entries per artist at $15 per piece, with a maximum of 2 works accepted. Cash awards for Best of Show/First Place, Second Place, and Honorable Mention. The online exhibition goes live August 10, 2026. — Deadline: July 26, 2026. Fee: $15/piece. Prize: Cash awards + Online exhibition.

item.title: The Summer National 2026 · Cape Cod Art Center
item.description: Open juried national all-media exhibition at Cape Cod Art Center in Barnstable, Massachusetts, photography included. Cash awards go to Best of Show plus First, Second, and Third Place in every medium drawing five or more entries, with a special Best Landscape award. Exhibition runs July 13 – August 14, 2026 at the center's galleries; accepted work is received July 13. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: $30/piece ($25 members). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Landscapes for Landsake 2026 · Agricultural Stewardship Association
item.description: 25th annual juried art sale and exhibition benefiting the Agricultural Stewardship Association, a land trust conserving farmland and forests in New York's Washington and Rensselaer counties. Work in 2D and 3D media — photography and print included — should draw inspiration from the agricultural landscapes, products, people, and rural life of the Taconic and Upper Hudson regions, traditional or interpretive. Around 300 works hang in the historic barn at Maple Ridge in Cambridge, NY, October 9–11, 2026, with an online exhibition continuing through November 15. Free to enter; participating artists donate 50% of proceeds to ASA's conservation work. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 59th Annual Newport Beach Art Exhibition
item.description: 59th annual juried exhibition and sale held in and around the Newport Beach Civic Center Community Room — a one-day show on August 15, 2026 with an awards reception at 4 p.m. Photography is its own award category alongside paintings, drawings and 3D art, with $300/$200/$100 prizes per category plus Juror's Choice and People's Choice. Up to two recently created original works per artist, hand-delivered; all work must be for sale with a 20% donation to the Newport Beach Arts Foundation on sales. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $35 ($50 for 2 works). Prize: $300/$200/$100 per category.

item.title: 44th Rock Island Art Guild Fine Arts Exhibition
item.description: Long-running juried exhibition presented with the Figge Art Museum in Davenport, Iowa, on view in the museum's fourth-floor gallery September 5, 2026 – January 10, 2027. Open to artists within a 200-mile radius of the Figge working in all media — photography, painting, sculpture, installation, sound, video, digital art and works on paper. Juried by Katherine Alcauskas, chief curator at the Chazen Museum of Art. $1,500/$750/$500 general awards plus watercolor and specialty awards. — Deadline: June 21, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: $1,500 + $750 + $500.

item.title: Kenmore Art Show 2026: Togetherness
item.description: Annual community juried show at Kenmore City Hall north of Seattle, themed 'Togetherness' for 2026 and inviting artists across the Pacific Northwest. Photography (film or digital) is one of four categories alongside 2D, 3D and the Little Gallery of small works. Per-category awards of $200/$150/$100 plus $300 Best in Show, $200 People's Choice and a Mayor's Purchase Award. Up to 2 pieces per category, hand-delivered; exhibition August 14–23, 2026. — Deadline: June 24, 2026. Fee: $25 ($15 2nd piece). Prize: $300 Best in Show + category awards.

item.title: Works on Paper · The Firefly Artists
item.description: National juried works-on-paper exhibition from Long Island artist cooperative The Firefly Artists, hung at the Darcy Arts Center in Northport, NY, July 21 – August 21, 2026. Photography is explicitly accepted alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, mixed media and digital media — original, human-made 2D works on paper up to 36"×36". First through third place and honorable mention awards; all work for sale with a 35% gallery commission. Reception August 6. — Deadline: June 27, 2026. Fee: $35 (+$5 each addl). Prize: Gallery exhibition + 1st-3rd place awards.

item.title: Peggy Doole National Small Works 2026 · Washington Print Foundation
item.description: 28th annual national small-works competition honoring printmaking advocate Peggy Doole, exhibited at Washington Printmakers Gallery in Washington, DC, July 30 – August 30, 2026. Accepts hand-pulled prints, screen prints, digital prints, fine art photographs and 3D work with print components — 2D work up to 250 square inches framed, made within the past two years. Juried by Washington art critic Mark Jenkins. $1,000 Grand Prize and $750 Washington Print Foundation Prize; reception August 1. — Deadline: July 3, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,000 Grand Prize + $750 WPF Prize.

item.title: 97th Michigan Contemporary Art Exhibition · Muskegon Museum of Art
item.description: 97th edition of the Muskegon Museum of Art's statewide juried exhibition, on view September 10 – November 4, 2026. Open to Michigan artists 18+ working in any medium except video and performance; photography and digital prints should be from limited editions. Up to two original works completed in the last two years. Juried by Detroit-born photographer Lauren Semivan (MFA, Cranbrook Academy of Art). Best of Show $1,500, second place $1,000, third place $750, plus additional prizes. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: $35 ($20 members). Prize: $1,500 + $1,000 + $750.

item.title: The Beauty of It · Old Town Arts & Crafts Guild
item.description: 8th annual juried competition from the Old Town Arts & Crafts Guild, a community gallery on Long Island's North Fork founded in 1948. Entries in three categories — Fine Art, Photography, and Mixed Media/Crafts — with $150/$100/$75 awards in each. Juried by artist Esther Marie Caponigro. Accepted work is exhibited and offered for sale in the Guild's virtual exhibition August 1 – September 30, 2026 (30% commission on sales). — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $25 (+$5 each addl). Prize: $150/$100/$75 per category.

item.title: Leigh Weimers Emerging Artists Awards 2026 · Rotary Club of San Jose
item.description: Annual unrestricted cash awards from the Rotary Club of San Jose honoring Mercury News columnist Leigh Weimers, for emerging artists whose work meaningfully engages or benefits residents of Santa Clara County (county residency itself not required). Visual arts including photography, plus music, literary and performance categories. Up to four winners receive grants that have ranged from $1,000 to $5,000 and present their work at the SJSU Hammer Theatre Center on October 21. Applicants should show some professional achievement but not yet wide recognition. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: Up to 4 grants of $1,000-$5,000.

item.title: Open Call: All Media 2026 · Studio Channel Islands
item.description: International juried exhibition in Studio Channel Islands' 3,000-square-foot gallery in Camarillo, California, August 1 – September 12, 2026. All media and styles welcome — including photography — for 2D/3D, video, film, performance, sound and installation work completed in the last three years; the prospectus asks for 'breakthrough pieces' that mark a turning point in your practice. Juried by Patricia Sweetow of Patricia Sweetow Gallery (Los Angeles). Cash prizes of $1,000/$750/$500 plus three juror's awards; 60/40 split on sales. — Deadline: July 7, 2026. Fee: $55 ($35 members). Prize: $1,000 + $750 + $500.

item.title: Kometa Fellows Program 2026
item.description: Fellowship from Kometa, the French magazine of on-the-ground reporting from zones of war, censorship, and political tension. Up to six fellows each receive €10,000 to complete a field-based project within one year, with monthly editorial support and an exclusivity agreement with the magazine. Open internationally to documentary photographers, photojournalists, journalists, and writers; this first 2026 call focuses on disinformation and narrative wars, and political and social change in the Gulf. Projects already under contract with a publisher are not eligible. A second call follows in winter 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €10,000 grant.

item.title: Betty Bowen Award 2026 · Seattle Art Museum
item.description: 49th annual Betty Bowen Award from the Seattle Art Museum for visual artists living and working in Washington, Oregon, or Idaho. The winner receives a $20,000 unrestricted cash prize and a solo exhibition at SAM; up to two Special Recognition Awards of $4,000 and three Special Commendation Awards of $2,500 are also given, and all finalists receive a $500 honorarium. First-round review by the Betty Bowen Committee is anonymous. All media accepted, including photography. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $20,000 + Solo exhibition at SAM.

item.title: Echoes: Revisiting Memory · Crooked Tree Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Crooked Tree Arts Center's Gilbert Gallery in Petoskey, Michigan, on memory engaged literally and metaphorically, juried by Paige Young, Assistant Professor of Photography at Kendall College of Art and Design. Open to artists 18+ in the Great Lakes region (Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, and Ontario). Cash awards of $500, $300, and $200; works must be from the past three years. Exhibition September 18 – October 31, 2026. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: $30 ($20 members). Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: Series: One Thing After Another · Site:Brooklyn Gallery
item.description: Online juried exhibition from Site:Brooklyn Gallery on contemporary seriality — how artists use series, repetition, and sequential approaches across all media. Juried by Matt Stromberg, freelance arts writer and educator contributing to Hyperallergic and the Los Angeles Times. Open internationally to artists 18+; all work must be for sale with a 60% artist commission. Exhibition online August 21 – September 21, 2026. — Deadline: July 27, 2026. Fee: $26 + $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Kinhouse: Exploring Kinship and the Spaces We Inhabit
item.description: National juried exhibition at Kinhouse Gallery & Residency in Fort Wayne, Indiana, seeking work on belonging, grounding, connection, and rootedness — with particular interest in the domestic sphere, caregiving, heritage, place, legacy, and community. Juried by Braydee Euliss, Indianapolis-based curator and founder of COMPANION gallery. Selected artists receive a $25 shipping stipend and possible inclusion in an extended exhibition catalog. Exhibition August 21 – September 30, 2026. — Deadline: June 28, 2026. Fee: $22. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog publication.

item.title: Transformation · Art Works Downtown
item.description: Juried exhibition at Art Works Downtown's 1337 Gallery in San Rafael, California, on the theme of transformation, juried by PJ Gubatina Policarpio, Curator at Root Division. Open to San Francisco Bay Area artists living within 100 miles of San Rafael; all visual media accepted, including photography. No giclées or reproductions. Exhibition August 7 – September 18, 2026. — Deadline: July 8, 2026. Fee: $40 (3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: CNY Artist Initiative 2027 · Everson Museum of Art
item.description: Competitive program at the Everson Museum of Art in Syracuse, New York: each year museum curators select regional artists for solo exhibitions in the Members' Council Gallery, running seven to nine weeks with accompanying programming such as artist talks and workshops. Open to artists living and working within a 75-mile radius of Syracuse. Selections are based on innovative quality, alignment with the museum's mission, and community relevance. 2027 exhibitions; apply with 20 images. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum solo exhibition.

item.title: Call for Exhibition Proposals · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Artlink Contemporary Gallery in Fort Wayne, Indiana, accepts proposals for solo, group, and curated exhibitions, reviewed once a year after March 1 by the Artlink Artist Panel and Exhibition Coordinator for the following year's schedule. Selected artists receive an exhibition contract and a flexible gallery space. Proposals are evaluated on concept, cohesiveness, innovation, craftsmanship, and accessibility. National artists welcome; shipping and travel are not covered. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: $25. Prize: Gallery exhibition.

item.title: Cyanotype: A Celebration of Process and Possibility · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont celebrating cyanotype in any form — traditional contact prints, camera-made cyanotypes, photograms, digital negatives, toned and wet cyanotypes, mixed media and experimental approaches, as long as cyanotype is the primary component of the finished work. Juried by Sam Wang. Up to 35 images selected for the gallery exhibition and 40 more for the online gallery; all selected work appears in the exhibition catalog and remains on the gallery website. Exhibition September 4–26, 2026, closing with World Cyanotype Day workshops and artist talks on September 26. Prints due August 21. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: $39 / 5 images + $6 each. Prize: Gallery + online exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Black & White Images — Photobook Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Open call from Treviso-based independent publisher Soft Publishing for black-and-white images of any subject — cohesive bodies of work or individual images. Up to 10 images per artist, minimum 2000px on one side, submitted with full captions (title, year, medium, dimensions) and a short description. Open to artists from anywhere and of all ages. Selected work is published in a limited-edition photobook. Entry €10 until July 10, €16 after; selected artists announced September 30, 2026. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: €10 (€16 after Jul 10). Prize: Publication.

item.title: The Black & White Show · Sacramento Fine Arts Center
item.description: All-media juried show at the Sacramento Fine Arts Center in Carmichael, California — submissions must be black, white, and greyscale only, including framing. Up to three pieces per artist ($25 each or three for $60; members $20/$50, youth $15/$40); work must be original and finished in the last three years. Digital art and photography explicitly accepted (files may be checked for AI). Judged by painter and former professional photographer Karen Burns. Best of Show receives a cash award and a solo exhibit at the center; other winners receive cash awards. Exhibition July 14 – August 8, 2026. — Deadline: June 18, 2026. Fee: $25 ($20 members). Prize: Cash awards + Best of Show solo exhibition.

item.title: 26th Annual Vivian & Stanley Reed Marine Show · Stamford Art Association
item.description: Multimedia juried exhibit from the Stamford Art Association on all things marine — the sea, the seashore, boats, activity on or near the water. Up to 9 works in any medium, from artists across disciplines and experience levels; up to $400 in awards given for excellence and conformity to the theme, with a 30% commission on sales. Entry is $35 for the first piece and $15 for each additional (members $30/$10). Named for Vivian and Stanley Reed, two founding SAA members and avid sailors. Hand delivery only (receiving July 10–11). Exhibition online and at the Townhouse Gallery July 16 – August 20, 2026, with opening reception July 16. — Deadline: June 26, 2026. Fee: $35 + $15 each addl ($30/$10 members). Prize: Up to $400 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Echoes of Place · Island Arts Council
item.description: Regional juried exhibition celebrating the historical tapestry of New Hanover County, North Carolina — from pre-colonial Indigenous presence through Civil War significance to modern coastal development. All media including photography; work must be original, made within the past three years, and inspired by the county. Open to artists 18+, up to two works per artist in each of the 2D and 3D categories; entry is $45 ($35 members, $20 students) and covers two pieces. All work must be for sale (25% commission). Exhibited August 1–15, 2026 at Fort Fisher State Historic Site, with select pieces chosen for extended display there afterwards. Juried by Gayle Tustin in consultation with historical consultant Dr. Jan Davidson. Awards include $1,000 for Historical Excellence, $750/$250/$100 in both 2D and 3D categories, and a People's Choice prize. Deadline extended from June 1 to June 15. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $45 ($35 members, $20 students). Prize: $1,000 top award + Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Lucent: The Art of Light · Artlink Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at Artlink Contemporary Gallery in Fort Wayne, Indiana exploring light in all media — from work that depicts light to work that emits it, interpreted broadly. Up to 10 samples; juried by Fort Wayne artist, curator and educator Ellen Mensch. Open to US artists 18+; work must be made within the last five years and not previously shown at Artlink. Exhibition July 30 – August 23, 2026; accepted work must arrive by July 19. 35% commission on sales. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $12 + $12 media fee. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Light/Shadow · Fig Tree Gallery
item.description: All-media juried exhibition at Fig Tree Gallery, the long-running artists' co-op in downtown Fresno, exploring the broad concept of light and its counterpart. 2–5 images of 2D or 3D work; photographic and digital work accepted printed on permanent media such as paper or canvas. Open to California artists 18+ who are not gallery members; work must be original, for sale, and made within the last three years. Exhibition September 3–27, 2026 with opening during Fresno's September 3 Art Hop; in-person delivery August 21–23. Juried by a five-artist panel; 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $45 + $5 media fee. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Essence of a Woman 2026 · MVA Gallery
item.description: National all-media call from MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, exploring the essence of a woman — her physical, psychological, and spiritual characteristics, from a simple portrait in tranquil repose to complex images of women performing personal and professional roles. Environmental portraits showing an individual in her surroundings are welcome. Photography is explicitly included alongside painting, printmaking, digital, sculpture, and more. Exhibition at MVA Gallery October 10 – November 7, 2026. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award carrying a future exhibition, and an annual Grand Prize NYC exhibition opportunity. $35 for 3 images, $5 each additional up to 9. Open to US artists 18+. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: $35/3 images. Prize: Exhibition + $200 Director's Choice.

item.title: Vehicles & Voyages · Arts Center East
item.description: Juried exhibition at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut celebrating the many ways we move through the world — cars, trucks, bicycles, motorcycles, boats, trains, aircraft, and the journeys they make possible. Historic vehicles, scenes of travel, personal road trips, maritime exploration, or imagined voyages into the future: movement, connection, freedom, and discovery. All media and artistic styles welcome, including photography; open to artists 18+. Entry $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), $5 each additional piece up to five. Shown August 8 – September 12, 2026, with reception and awards August 22. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: $35–$55. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Dog Days of Summer · WHAM Art Association
item.description: WHAM Art Center in Surprise, Arizona invites artists to respond to the hottest, stillest stretch of the season — the dog days, named for the rise of Sirius, the Dog Star, at the peak of summer heat. Sought: work that captures what summer at its peak feels like — heat, stillness, nostalgia, exhaustion, memory, and atmosphere — through color, landscape, abstraction, or personal storytelling. All media welcome, including photography; works may be literal, abstract, symbolic, or conceptual. Entry $40 for up to five entries (a related series counts as one); all work must be for sale, 25% gallery commission. Exhibition runs August 4–29, 2026. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: TSHOW.2 · Tyler Art Lift
item.description: Second edition of TSHOW, the international juried exhibition from Texas nonprofit Tyler Art Lift. Open to painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking and photography up to 80×80 inches — a chance for photographers to show alongside other media with serious cash on the line: $3,000 Best in Show, $1,500 runner-up and a $500 People's Choice award chosen by visitors. Exhibition at Gallery Main Street in downtown Tyler, Texas, September 23 – October 10, 2026, with opening reception October 3. Open internationally to artists 18+; $45 for the first entry, $5 each additional; 30% sales commission supports the show. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $45 (1 work). Prize: $3,000 / $1,500 / $500.

item.title: Chew on This · Ludington Area Center for the Arts
item.description: Food-themed juried exhibition at the Ludington Area Center for the Arts on the Lake Michigan shore, inviting artists to explore the creative, cultural and visual power of food — from realistic depictions to conceptual pieces about consumption and community. 'If it involves food — or is inspired by it — we want to see it.' All media welcome including photography, collage, drawing, painting, sculpture, ceramics, fiber and installation. On view at the LACA Gallery October 2–31, 2026. Open to artists 18+ nationally and internationally; $30 for up to two works; 30% commission for members, 45% for non-members. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Keller Prize 2026
item.description: Annual international all-media art competition founded in 2022 by artist Shelly Hamill in honor of her grandmother, Texas landscape painter Jane Keller. Open to painting, photography, sculpture, drawing, printmaking, textile art, installation and mixed media; juried in 2026 by Aspen gallerist Mia Valley of Valley Fine Art. Cash prizes of $5,000 grand prize, $2,500 first runner-up and $1,500 second runner-up; past grand prize winners include painter Andrea Kowch (2025). All submissions appear in the online gallery, and winners are spotlighted in Architectural Digest. Open internationally to artists 18+; $55 for five images, $7 each additional up to 15. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $55 (5 images). Prize: $5,000 + $2,500 + $1,500.

item.title: Eleventh Juried Art Show · Stover Mill Gallery
item.description: Eleventh juried exhibition at the Stover Mill Gallery in Erwinna — Bucks County's longest continually running art gallery, now in its 66th season, owned and maintained by the nonprofit Tinicum Civic Association. Open to all media including photography (no giclée reproductions); one work per artist, maximum 36 inches framed. More than $3,000 in prize money awarded through a blind jury process judging artistic excellence and aesthetic vision. Shown over four weekends October 17 – November 8, 2026, with a reception October 18; accepted artists may also offer two unframed portfolio pieces for sale. All works must be for sale; 30% commission supports the gallery. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Over $3,000 in prizes.

item.title: Photo Folio Review 2026 · Les Rencontres d'Arles
item.description: Official portfolio review programme of Les Rencontres d'Arles, held July 6–10, 2026 during the festival's opening week at the Maison de la vie associative. One-on-one 20-minute sessions with international experts — curators, editors, publishers, and festival directors. Packages run from 5 appointments (€200) to 20 (€550). Each year the experts vote for their favorite portfolio and select a Photo Folio Review Award winner, whose work is presented at the following edition — the 2024 winner Patrick Wack exhibited at Arles 2025. Online reservations only, open until midnight June 18 (Paris time), subject to availability. — Deadline: June 18, 2026. Fee: €200–€550. Prize: Portfolio reviews + Exhibition.

item.title: TOKAS Research Residency Program 2027
item.description: Research-focused residency at Tokyo Arts and Space for international and local creators — visual artists (photographers welcome), designers, architects, curators, critics, and writers. Five places for 6–12 week stays within one of three periods between May 2027 and March 2028, for conducting research on arts and culture in Tokyo. TOKAS provides a single-room living space at TOKAS Residency in Koto-ku; no studio or workspace is included. No age limit; applicants must not be students at the time of participation; duos may apply. Application package PDF plus online form with two letters of recommendation and a portfolio. Deadline June 16, 2026, 18:00 JST. — Deadline: June 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 6–12 week residency + Accommodation.

item.title: Lanesboro Exhibition Gallery 2028
item.description: Lanesboro Arts' Exhibition Gallery in Lanesboro, Minnesota programs three to four solo artist exhibitions a year, each running roughly eight weeks. Applications are open for the gallery's 2028 exhibition series; all visual arts media are eligible, including photography. Artists must reside in Minnesota, Wisconsin, or Iowa. Showing work for sale is optional, at a 60% consignment rate to the artist. Online applications preferred; video applications accepted by email. Notification by February 26, 2027. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 8-week solo exhibition.

item.title: Lanesboro Early Career Artists Show 2027
item.description: Group exhibition highlighting the work of three or more early career artists from Minnesota, Iowa, or Wisconsin at the Lanesboro Arts Gallery, February 6 – March 20, 2027. Lanesboro Arts defines an early career artist as one with great potential who has not yet established significant gallery representation. All visual arts media welcome, including photography. Applications due December 7, 2026 at 12 pm noon; accepted artists contacted by December 23. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Her Art, Her Voice — 2027 Biennial Juried Exhibition · New Mexico State Committee of NMWA
item.description: Biennial juried exhibition of the New Mexico State Committee of the National Museum of Women in the Arts, co-hosted by Turner Carroll Gallery and GF Contemporary on Canyon Road, Santa Fe, March 5 – April 3, 2027. Open to women-identifying artists residing in New Mexico who are NMC-NMWA members with an Artist Registry page (or registry information submitted by August 31, 2026). All mediums and subject matters considered, including photography. Awards include Best of Show, Award of Excellence, Award of Merit, and two Honorable Mentions. $50 for up to three artworks. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $50. Prize: Exhibition + Best of Show award.

item.title: agriCultural: A Biennial Exhibition · New Bedford Art Museum
item.description: Juried biennial presented by the Southeastern Massachusetts Agricultural Partnership (SEMAP) and the New Bedford Art Museum, investigating the complex and undertold stories of agriculture, farming, and the contemporary stories held in the land. Seeks work from artists who are farmers, farmers who are artists, and artists deeply engaged with agricultural themes — 2D and 3D media welcome, including photography. Open to artists residing in Massachusetts or Rhode Island. On view September 10 – November 29, 2026 at the New Bedford Art Museum. — Deadline: June 26, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Space: Negative, Outer, Living · Arts Center East
item.description: Juried exhibition at Arts Center East in Vernon, Connecticut inviting artists to explore the many meanings of space — physical, emotional, imagined, and infinite. From the vast mystery of outer space to the quiet structure of negative space in composition and the personal environments we inhabit every day: distance, atmosphere, architecture, isolation, balance, discovery, and the relationships between objects and the spaces around them. All media and artistic perspectives welcome, including photography; open to artists 18+. Entry $35 for one piece ($30 for ACE members), rising per additional piece up to five. Shown in the Marmer Gallery, August 8 – September 12, 2026. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: $35–$55. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Vision 250: America in Harmony · WHAM Art Association
item.description: WHAM Art Center in Surprise, Arizona invites artists to celebrate America's 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence with a special exhibition exploring freedom, harmony, and vision. In a time of division and polarization, the show asks: what would a unified, creative, and harmonious America look like — an America where differences are met with curiosity and connection? All media welcome, including photography; the show will highlight artwork by veterans. Entry $40 for up to five entries (a related series counts as one); exhibition runs July 2–30, 2026. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Pop Art Exhibition · Sparks Gallery
item.description: Sparks Gallery in San Diego's Gaslamp Quarter is hosting a Pop Art exhibition showcasing bold, contemporary works inspired by popular culture and modern life. Submissions should reflect Pop Art's playful, colorful, or critical style, exploring themes like consumerism, celebrity culture, comics, and nostalgia — both traditional and innovative approaches welcome, including photography. Open to U.S.-based artists; work must be original and for sale. $20 entry plus $10 per additional media. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $20+. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist in Focus · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Open call from Fotografiska Emerging and Fotografiska Berlin inspired by Anton Corbijn, running alongside the Berlin museum's Corbijn retrospective. Submit a cover-worthy portrait of an artist or creative voice whose character shines through in a single frame — portraits that go beyond appearance and reveal something honest and memorable about the subject. Lens-based photography only; AI-generated images excluded. One image per submission, up to three submissions per photographer. Three selected artists each receive a signed copy of the 'Corbijn, Anton' photobook, Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3 headphones, and Instagram features on the Fotografiska Berlin and Emerging accounts. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Signed Corbijn photobook + B&W headphones.

item.title: Art Shapes the Future · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Open call from Fotografiska Emerging in partnership with IFA Berlin and Volkswagen R, inviting emerging image-makers to submit work that looks ahead: how technology shapes society, human-technology relationships, and emerging realities. Documentary, conceptual, and experimental approaches all welcome — lens-based photography, video, and prompt-based AI work accepted. Three selected artists each receive €1,500, exhibition at the Creator Hub during IFA Berlin (September 4–8, 2026), an Instagram collaboration post with Volkswagen R, IFA, and Fotografiska Berlin & Emerging, and a platform feature. Juried by representatives of Volkswagen R Design, IFA management, and Fotografiska. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,500 + IFA Berlin exhibition.

item.title: Skyway 2027: A Contemporary Collaboration
item.description: Triennial exhibition centering artists shaping contemporary art in the Tampa Bay region, co-organized by five museums: the Museum of Fine Arts St. Petersburg, The John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art, Sarasota Art Museum of Ringling College, Tampa Museum of Art, and USF Contemporary Art Museum. Open to artists and collectives working in all media — photography included — who live in Hillsborough, Manatee, Pasco, Pinellas, or Sarasota counties. Selected artists exhibit at one of the five venues between March and fall 2027 and are featured in a full-color catalog with curatorial essays. Free to apply with up to 10 images (plus optional video). — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Fashion Regenerated 2026 · Textile Exchange
item.description: Photography and filmmaking competition from Textile Exchange, the global nonprofit driving sustainable fiber and material production, in partnership with Atmos. Visual storytellers are invited to document regeneration across the fashion, textile, and apparel industry — from fiber cultivation to circular design. The overall winner receives a $10,000 paid commission to create new work documenting regeneration, publication through Atmos and Textile Exchange, and an exhibition at the 2026 Textile Exchange Conference; two runners-up receive $2,000 each plus promotion and conference display. Open to photographers and filmmakers 18+ of any nationality; winners must be available to travel autumn 2026 – summer 2027 for the commission. Submit up to 25 photographs, a short film, or both. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 commission + 2×$2,000 + Publication + Exhibition.

item.title: BBA 360 — Online Exhibition 2026
item.description: Open call from Berlin's BBA Gallery for its 360° digital exhibition format. Open to artists and photographers 18+ worldwide working in any medium except video and sculpture, with no theme restrictions. Around 45 artworks are featured in the immersive 360° online gallery; 15 shortlisted artists are additionally presented in an online group show with Artsy profiles and promotion through BBA channels. The first-prize winner receives a cash award, an Artsy profile, and a physical exhibition at BBA Gallery in Berlin in 2026/27. €29 fee covers up to 5 works; no shipping required for the online round. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: €29. Prize: Cash prize + Exhibition + Artsy profile.

item.title: Willet Art Prize 2026
item.description: Free national art competition from Willet Studios, the storied American stained glass studio founded in 1898. The 2026 theme, 'Quest for Gold,' invites work exploring movement, strength, determination, and the human pursuit of excellence in sport. Any medium is accepted and all experience levels are welcome — entries are judged on creativity, theme interpretation, composition, emotional impact, and suitability for translation into glass. Prizes of $7,000, $2,000, and $1,000 from a $10,000 total pool; winning designs may be developed into stained glass pieces with per-sale commissions to the artist for up to three years. One original work per artist, not previously exhibited. Open to US residents 18+; winners announced October 2026. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 + $7,000 + $2,000.
